Simplest model: time ≈ fixed (~0.15 s, partly removable) + steps × per-step cost. Per-step cost is pixel-proportional plus a large memory-bound component on the 31×31 maps (whitening output and group 1: BN/GELU/pool). Accuracy rises slowly with total steps, about 0.2 pp per 0.5 epoch, costing roughly 1.5–2.7 s/pp. The tip (E036) is 5.31 s at 0.7532 on seeds 0–2. Held-out is probably about 0.752–0.753, so headroom over the 0.75 bar is thin.

Mechanisms, with supporting experiments:
1. Early low resolution is cheap (E026, E033). The 32 px tail and the 3×3 final-map regime carry accuracy (E011, E018, E024).
2. Memory-bound cuts save more than their MAC share (E028, E034, E036). An annealed group-1 LR makes the freeze nearly free in accuracy. Group-1 and whitening backward is the main lever. Deeper freeze, BN folding and the whitening-bias stop are the same family, with diminishing returns. E036 saved about 0.13 s after E035's 0.03 s, and accuracy dropped only about 0.15 pp (E035 to E036).
3. Averaging, LS and warmup tweaks (E025, E029, E030, E032) are null or negative. The recipe sits at a local optimum, and changes cost 0.3–0.7 pp.
4. wd ×0.5 helped about 0.2 pp (E016). Muon's gain is confounded with batch size and an RNG re-draw (E006).
5. Systems work is worth about 1% each (CUDA graphs E015, prepare cost E035).
6. Sample dropping (E031) saves time proportionally but costs about 0.4 pp, which is worse than the epoch dial.

Noise: 3-seed accuracy SE is about 0.1–0.15 pp. Held-out 10-seed SE is about 0.06 pp. Time noise is about ±0.03 s. Any RNG change re-rolls seeds 0–2. Selection on seeds 3–12 carries a winner's curse of about 0.05–0.1 pp.

Misses so far: I underestimated the memory-bound savings (freeze and early 20 px), and I overestimated how far averaging and LS tweaks could help.

Unsure: the held-out mean of the tip; PCIe transfer of the memory-bound levers; how deep the freeze can go (60%). The whitening bias already stops at 20%, so that lever is now taken.

forecasts.reason: Saves about 0.1 s, but accuracy is already at the bar, so the cost likely exceeds the 0.1 pp allowance.
The diagnostic is likely to show a fresh-seed mean near 0.752–0.753, with winner's-curse shrinkage.
BN stats on the 31×31 maps are memory-bound and worth about 1.5%, but the fold complexity adds some risk of small accuracy drift.
No recipe change; the profile will likely show non-GEMM kernels at 30% or more of the step.
Muon likely beats SGD by 0.2–0.5 pp, and SGD is slightly cheaper per step.

cruxes: What is the true held-out (fresh-seed) mean of the tip? If it is below 0.752, further time cuts need an accuracy lever first.
Does the accuracy cost of a deeper freeze (60%) stay under 0.1 pp?
What share of the 32 px step is bandwidth-bound BN/GELU/pool, and does it transfer to the PCIe judge?
